progress.text: Windows installer: the Start menu shortcut takes the icon embedded in deckcraft.exe instead of an MSI <Icon>, so a taskbar pin keeps its icon after an update (#1114); a pin that already lost it has to be unpinned and pinned again once

AutoFormat as you type: a paragraph that starts with , -, --, >, <>, 1., 1), I., i., A., a. or a) and a space or tab becomes a bulleted or numbered list in that style; Backspace right after puts the typed text back, and Tools ▸ AutoCorrect and text.autocorrect {lists} turn it off

Tables: while the caret is in a cell, dragging into another cell selects that range of cells (shaded, merged cells taken in whole), and Shift+arrow grows or shrinks it; formatting applies to the selected cells only, and Delete clears their text and keeps the table

Preferences ▸ Measurement units: inches or centimetres. The Format pane's Size and Position fields, Shape Format ▸ Size on the ribbon, the Slide Size dialog and the ruler show and take the chosen unit; the deck still stores points (#1326)

A picture's own fill shows behind its transparent pixels, and an embedded object (an old equation, p:oleObj) takes the fill and outline of its fallback picture, as PowerPoint for Mac draws them (synthetic probe: a half-transparent PNG on orange and on yellow with an outline); on a private 166-deck corpus 51 slides of equations on coloured boxes move closer to PowerPoint's PDF, none further

Columns dialog: Home › Columns › More Columns… and Format Shape › Text Box › Columns… set the number of text columns (1 to 16) and the spacing between them in inches, in one undo step; format.columns with no fields opens it, and a key left out keeps the text box's own value

Slide Show: Ctrl+wheel (Cmd+wheel on a Mac) over the slide zooms in and out around the pointer, four notches per doubling, up to 4×, as in PowerPoint; zooming back to the whole slide leaves the zoom, and the plain wheel still turns the page (#1286)

Format Shape and Format Background ▸ Pattern fill: a gallery of the 48 preset patterns PowerPoint offers, drawn in the current colors, with Foreground and Background color menus. Format Shape could only set 25 % in accent 1 on background 1, and Format Background listed 10 presets by their XML names

Edit Points: hold Shift, Ctrl or Alt while dragging a point's handle to make it a smooth, straight or corner point, as in PowerPoint (Cmd and Option work as Ctrl and Alt on the Mac); the point keeps that type for the next drag
Edit Points: Esc pressed before the mouse button is released cancels a point or handle drag, as in PowerPoint, and leaves the shape as it was with no undo step. Edit Points stays on after the cancel
Edit Points: right-click a segment for Add Point (at the pointer), Delete Segment (a closed outline opens there; grayed out on an open one) and Open/Close Path, as in PowerPoint (shape.deleteSegment)

Chart text colour: chart.options {textColor} and Font Color on a selected chart colour its title, axes, legend and data labels; the colour is written to the chart part (c:txPr on the axes, legend, labels and chart, the title's run defaults) so an imported chart keeps its txPr colours through an edit and a save; text without a colour of its own takes PowerPoint's default, the theme's text colour at 65 % plus 35 % (595959 on a light theme, light grey on a dark one)
Format Background ▸ Apply to All also sets the background of the slide masters the slides use (and clears their layouts' overrides), so new slides keep it (#891)
A shape with no fill and no line (a text box) no longer draws its shape-level glow as a halo round its box; the text's own glow is all PowerPoint shows
Normal view: a slide zoomed past the window gets a horizontal and a vertical scroll bar on the axes that overflow; drag the thumb or click the track to reach every edge (#1157)

Table text takes the master's other-text style (otherStyle), shapes and text boxes the presentation's default text style, as PowerPoint for Mac draws them (synthetic probe: 14 pt cells under a 14 pt otherStyle and a 26 pt defaultTextStyle); a private deck's table had been drawn 20 pt instead of 18

Slide Show: while animations play, each frame draws only the slide's shapes over the slide's backdrop (background, master and layout graphics), rendered once and ahead of time. A full-slide picture with a glow in the layout re-rendered at every frame held animations to 2–3 frames a second (~390 ms a frame at 1080p); now ~28 ms

Animation Pane ▸ Play From: with an effect selected, the pane's play button starts the canvas preview at that effect, with the effects before it already played. With nothing selected it is still Play All
Shape Fill and Shape Outline format the members of a selected group, including nested groups, in one undo step. Fill transparency retains each member's effective colour (#1079)

Chart bars and their legend keys draw the series' own pattern fill (a:pattFill, now read and written) and draw nothing for a:noFill, with the series outline where it has one, as PowerPoint for Mac does (synthetic probe); they took the palette's colour before. Lines, areas and markers use a pattern's foreground colour

Opening a .pptx puts the text of shapes without an anchor at the top even when the theme's shape defaults (spDef) centre new shapes, as PowerPoint for Mac draws them; checked with a synthetic probe and on a private 166-deck corpus (51 slides closer to PowerPoint's PDF, none further)

3-D contours, extrusion depths and bevels keep their size in points inside a group whose child coordinates scale its shapes: a 1 pt contour on a small extruded cube in a legacy group drew hundreds of points wide, a band across the slide

Groups nest at most 32 deep (arrange.group refuses more), as deep as PPTX import reads and slides draw: a deck grouped 39 or more levels deep saved without complaint and then could not be opened again

Review › Language has Whole presentation: one proofing language for every text box, table cell, note, master and layout, and the default for new text (format.languageAll, one undo step); the per-selection language still works
Reuse Slides: pick which slides of the other presentation to insert from a list (slide.reuseList, #1103)
Slide list and slide sorter: Shift+click selects a range of slides and Ctrl+Shift+click adds it to the selection (slide.selectRange, #1105)

Chart number formats with explicit empty positive, negative or zero sections hide the corresponding labels, including all values with three semicolons; a blank whole format still uses General. Synthetic formatter regressions
Tests: the Options dialog's Cancel, Esc and close button put the settings back the way they were (#878)
Tests: Ctrl+A in the slide sorter selects every slide, as in PowerPoint (#936)

README: the Linux runtime libraries a tarball or musl install has to provide — the dlopened X11/Vulkan/GL/dialog libraries with their Alpine and Void package names, the software-Vulkan fallback, and why fontconfig and freetype are not among them (#955)
Find (Ctrl+F): "Find what:" has the keyboard as soon as the dialog opens, and keeps it after Enter finds a match, so the search can be typed and changed without clicking the field (#951)
Duplicate (Ctrl+D) repeats a move: duplicate a shape, move the copy, and the next Duplicate places its copy the same distance further on, as in PowerPoint (#966)

Native chart sidecar bytes move from JSON arrays into referenced ZIP entries, with shared media byte/item limits and bounded reads; older inline sidecars still load. Synthetic format regressions cover large workbooks and malformed members
Slide thumbnails and the Slide Sorter render only the slides in view: on a deck of more than 600 slides they used to evict their own thumbnails, so the pane flashed white and never finished (#969)

Resizing with the mouse snaps the edge being dragged to the slide, guides and other shapes: a fixed edge that already lined up used to take the snap and leave the dragged edge free, and a fixed edge near a line shifted the dragged one (#961)
Slide show: a video or audio clip is looked up on the slide it belongs to, so slides whose shape ids repeat (the PPTX import numbers each slide afresh) no longer play each other's clips (#994)
About: Contributors and Models get their own fixed-size block below the tab row, so the tab row is no longer squeezed into the credits and the tabs keep answering (#843)
Charts: a series' own data-label setting is honoured — numbers PowerPoint shows on a graph no longer disappear, and a bare c:showVal means on (#868)
Thumbnails: navigating slides with the arrow keys scrolls the thumbnail pane to keep the current slide visible (#917)

Opening a file caps absurd effect sizes (glow, soft edges, shadows, reflections, on shapes, text and table text) at what Format Shape allows: a glow of 10^18 pt in a .pptx made rendering ask for 34 GB and abort
